title: Standardized Compliance Documentation
summary: This cluster represents the standardized templates (certificates and undertakings) used by importers to certify the use of machinery in industrial processes (BMR/BMRE). These documents remain functionally static as they serve as recurring administrative requirements for customs clearance.

timeline.change: Standardized administrative templates for industrial machinery import certification.

Bangladesh Poultry Industries Associatio: The association acts as an endorsing body by certifying that an industrial entity is a registered member and its imported goods are intended for production purposes.

The association provides formal recommendations to the customs authority for the application of concessional duty rates on imported machinery, parts, and materials based on the relevant statutory regulatory order.
S.R.O. 178-AIN/2010: This statutory regulatory order provides the legal basis for granting concessional duty rates on the import of specific industrial machinery, equipment, and raw materials used in production processes.
Board of Investment: The Board of Investment serves as the official registration authority for textile-related industrial enterprises seeking to avail of specified fiscal concessions.

Customs Act 1969: This legal instrument establishes the regulatory framework and penalties for the import of industrial machinery and equipment under specific operational conditions.
It mandates that in the event of misuse of imported goods, the importer is liable to pay standard duties and taxes and accept any additional penalties imposed by the Customs Authority under the Act.
Customs Authority: This body is responsible for enforcing compliance and applying legal penalties to importers who fail to adhere to the stated conditions for the utilization of industrial machinery and equipment.

Textile Industry: A registered textile industry may import machinery, spare parts, and raw materials for the purpose of balancing, modernization, replacement, and expansion (BMRE) of their industrial units.
The industry must verify the use of imported goods through a formal certificate to justify the release or return of their submitted undertakings or bonds.
Board of Investment: Industrial establishments involved in textile manufacturing must be registered with the Board of Investment to qualify for specific industrial import benefits.
Bill of Entry: The import of industrial machinery and equipment is linked to specific customs documentation, such as the bill of entry, which serves as evidence of the imported goods used in industrial projects.
Balancing, Modernization, Replacement, a: The BMRE process refers to the formal scheme under which industrial entities are permitted to upgrade their operational capacity through the import of machinery and spare parts.

Customs Act 1969: This legal instrument authorizes customs authorities to impose penalties for the misuse of imported industrial machinery, spare parts, or materials beyond the standard duties and taxes applicable.
Industrial Importation: Importers must provide a formal declaration pledging that goods imported under specific commercial documents will be utilized exclusively for the installation, replacement, balancing, modernization, or expansion of industrial facilities.
Any deviation from the stated industrial purpose renders the importer liable to pay standard customs duties and taxes and subjects them to further enforcement actions under existing customs laws.

Customs Act 1969: This act empowers the customs authority to impose and collect duties and taxes on imported goods.
It provides the legal framework under which customs authorities can penalize parties for failure to comply with the declared conditions of use for imported industrial equipment and components.
Customs Authority: The customs authority is responsible for enforcing the regulatory requirements and conditions associated with the importation of industrial machinery and equipment.
They have the legal power to recover standard duty and tax rates and impose penalties in the event of non-compliance with the established industrial usage terms.
Industrial Equipment and Spare Parts: These goods are subject to specific conditions when imported for purposes such as establishment, replacement, balancing, modernization, or expansion (BMRE) of an industrial unit.
Importers must provide an undertaking that these imported items will be strictly utilized for the designated industrial projects or face potential fiscal and legal consequences.
